title: Frontend: Pin Items
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Pin Items. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App({items=[A,B,C]}). Pin buttons[data-pin=LABEL] toggle pinned membership. Render li[data-row=LABEL] with pinned rows first, preserving original relative order in each partition. Output comma-joined order in [data-testid=order]. Labels are unique.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Store pinned IDs separately from the underlying records.
alternativeApproaches: Synchronize pin preferences across devices with versioned updates instead of index-based writes.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Pin/unpin; repeated pin; filtered pinned item.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
